Schema:
-- WiKi database model - DuckDB.
--
-- This is the structure load_duckdb.py builds out of the wpars output. The
-- loader creates the tables itself with CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT,
-- so this file is not needed to load data; it is the written-down model of the
-- result, and it stands up an empty database with the same tables for tooling
-- that expects them to exist.
--
-- Run it with the DuckDB CLI. The ATTACH names the database file, so the file
-- does not have to be on the command line - both of these end up in the same
-- place:
--
--   duckdb < db_model.sql              -- creates ./wiki.duckdb
--   duckdb wiki.duckdb < db_model.sql  -- same database, already open
--
-- Every table is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so running this against a loaded
-- database changes nothing and cannot drop rows.
--
-- The MySQL version of this model was replaced when the project moved to
-- DuckDB; it is in git history as `git show 7febd4b:db_model.sql`. Its column
-- widths no longer hold anyway - labels run past VARCHAR(30) and `year` needs
-- more than SMALLINT (see the note on events below).
--
-- No table carries a primary key, a foreign key or an index:
--   - the CSVs are the source of truth and every load rebuilds the tables, so
--     constraints would only slow the bulk load down;
--   - the workload is analytical (group by century, filter by occupation or
--     country, join events to items), which DuckDB answers by scanning columns
--     with zone maps rather than by seeking through an index.
-- The relationships are written in the comments instead. They hold: the
-- January extract had 0 orphans in events, attributes and item_classes.

ATTACH IF NOT EXISTS 'wiki.duckdb' AS wiki;
USE wiki;


-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- Dictionaries
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per selected Wikidata item: everything that has at least one date
-- and belongs to at least one class of interest. Source: ItemsExt.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (
    qid             VARCHAR,  -- Wikidata QID, e.g. Q42
    "label"         VARCHAR,  -- English label
    description     VARCHAR,
    label_ru        VARCHAR,  -- second language, see get_sites() in gconfig.h
    description_ru  VARCHAR
);

-- Property dictionary, tagged with the role the property plays here.
-- Source: properties.json plus the two selection files.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS properties (
    pid          VARCHAR,  -- e.g. P569
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. date of birth
    description  VARCHAR,
    kind         VARCHAR   -- 'date' | 'attribute' | 'other'
);

-- The P31 whitelist: every class reachable from a seed through P279, tagged
-- with the domain(s) that seed belongs to. Built by build_class_closure.py.
-- Source: select_classes.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS classes (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR,
    domains      VARCHAR   -- '|' separated, e.g. 'event|literature|music'.
                           -- A closed set of seven tags, one per seed group:
                           -- art, event, literature, music, person, place,
                           -- science. Any other value matches nothing.
);

-- Labels for the QIDs that turn up as attribute values (occupations,
-- countries, places, genres). Resolved out of the full item dump by
-- resolve_values.py, because those items are not selected in their own right.
-- Source: values.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS value_items (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR
);


-- Which area each occupation belongs to. A question says "scientists" and P106
-- records a profession: the 15th century has 58,088 dated people, of whom 50
-- are labelled "scientist" and the rest are astronomers, physicians and
-- mathematicians. Built by build_occupation_areas.py from the P279 closure of a
-- few area roots, kept to the occupations the extract actually uses.
-- Source: occupation_areas.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS occupation_areas (
    qid          VARCHAR,  -- the QID a P106 attribute row points at
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. astronomer
    areas        VARCHAR,  -- '|' separated: art, literature, music, science
    people       BIGINT    -- how many people in the extract hold it
);


-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- Facts
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per (item, date property, class) fact - the events the questions are
-- asked about. Source: DataEvents.csv, loaded with DISTINCT.
--
-- The Wikidata time string is kept as it arrived and also split into columns,
-- since the questions are about years and centuries.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    qid            VARCHAR,   -- -> items.qid
    property       VARCHAR,   -- -> properties.pid, e.g. P569 (date of birth)
    "class"        VARCHAR,   -- -> classes.qid
    time_raw       VARCHAR,   -- as in the dump, e.g. +1991-02-12T00:00:00Z
    "year"         BIGINT,    -- signed. Not SMALLINT: 40 rows in the January
                              -- extract were already outside 16 bits. Not even
                              -- INTEGER: the Big Bang is -13800000000.
    "month"        UTINYINT,  -- 0 when the source has no month precision
    "day"          UTINYINT,  -- 0 when the source has no day precision
    bc             BOOLEAN,   -- true for a negative year, e.g. Caesar -0044
    timezone       INTEGER,
    qual_property  VARCHAR,   -- claim qualifier, nullable
    qual_value     VARCHAR    -- nullable
);

-- Non-date claims: occupation, citizenship, place of birth, genre and the rest
-- of attribute_properties.csv. One row per (item, property, value) - an item
-- with three occupations has three rows. Source: Attributes.csv, DISTINCT.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attributes (
    qid       VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    property  VARCHAR,  -- -> properties.pid
    "value"   VARCHAR   -- -> value_items.qid
);

-- Which classes an item belongs to. Separate from events because an item is
-- normally an instance of several classes, and a question can arrive through
-- any of them. Source: ItemClasses.csv, DISTINCT.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS item_classes (
    qid      VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    "class"  VARCHAR   -- -> classes.qid
);

-- Wikipedia presence per item. sitelinks is the notability signal used to rank
-- answers - it is the only one the dump offers - and the titles are the join
-- key to article text, should the Wikipedia dataset be pulled in later.
-- Source: ItemSites.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sites (
    qid        VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    sitelinks  INTEGER,  -- number of Wikipedia editions holding the item
    enwiki     VARCHAR,  -- English article title, NULL when there is none
    ruwiki     VARCHAR   -- Russian article title, NULL when there is none
);


-- What the database holds now. Zero rows everywhere means the tables were just
-- created and the loader has not run yet.
SELECT table_name, estimated_size AS rows, column_count AS columns
FROM duckdb_tables()
WHERE database_name = 'wiki'
ORDER BY table_name;


Examples:
-- Example queries against the DuckDB database built by load_duckdb.py.
--
-- Run the whole file, or open the database and paste one query at a time:
--
--   duckdb wiki.duckdb < queries.sql
--   duckdb wiki.duckdb
--
-- The Python library in /home/denis/projects/venv3.11 opens the same file
-- (both are v1.5.5, the storage format is tied to the version):
--
--   >>> import duckdb
--   >>> duckdb.connect('wiki.duckdb').sql("<paste a query>").show()
--
-- Tables: items, events, attributes, item_classes, sites, value_items,
-- classes, occupation_areas, properties - the model is in db_model.sql.
-- Queries 1 and 2 run on any build; the rest need attributes and item_classes,
-- which only exist after a run made with --attrs.


-- 1. What happened in a given year in music and science.
--    Items are matched through every class they belong to, and classes carry
--    the domain tag assigned by build_class_closure.py.
SELECT i.label,
       i.description,
       c.label   AS class,
       c.domains AS area,
       p.label   AS date_type,
       e.year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
JOIN properties p   ON p.pid = e.property
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND (c.domains LIKE '%music%' OR c.domains LIKE '%science%')
ORDER BY c.domains, i.label;


-- 2. The same question asked over a whole century, counted by area.
SELECT (e.year / 100)::BIGINT * 100 AS century,
       c.domains AS area,
       count(DISTINCT e.qid) AS items
FROM events e
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1800 AND 1899
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY items DESC;


-- 3. Which scientists lived in Germany in the 1400s.
--    "Lived in" is read as born or died inside the window, which also keeps
--    people whose other date is unknown.
WITH lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
),
occupation AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS occupation
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P106'
),
citizenship AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS country
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P27'
)
-- a person usually has several occupations and sometimes several
-- citizenships, so collapse them instead of repeating the person per row
SELECT i.label,
       string_agg(DISTINCT o.occupation, ', ') AS occupations,
       string_agg(DISTINCT z.country, ', ')    AS countries,
       min(l.born) AS born,
       min(l.died) AS died
FROM lifespan l
JOIN items i      USING (qid)
JOIN occupation o USING (qid)
JOIN citizenship z USING (qid)
WHERE z.country ILIKE '%German%'
  -- "scientist" is an area, not a job title - only 50 people dated to this
  -- century carry it, against 2,039 professions that occupation_areas puts
  -- under science
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attributes a
              JOIN occupation_areas oa ON oa.qid = a."value"
              WHERE a.qid = l.qid AND a.property = 'P106'
                AND list_contains(str_split(oa.areas, '|'), 'science'))
  AND (l.born BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499 OR l.died BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499)
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY born;


-- 4. Anyone by occupation and period, the generic form of query 3.
--    Change the two parameters at the top and the rest follows.
WITH params AS (SELECT 'composer' AS want_occupation, 1700 AS from_year, 1799 AS to_year),
lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
)
SELECT i.label, v.label AS occupation, l.born, l.died
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
JOIN items i       ON i.qid = a.qid
JOIN lifespan l    ON l.qid = a.qid
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
  AND v.label = params.want_occupation
  AND l.born BETWEEN params.from_year AND params.to_year
ORDER BY l.born;


-- 5. Musical works of a year with the people and genre attached to them.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P86'  THEN v.label END) AS composer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P175' THEN v.label END) AS performer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P136' THEN v.label END) AS genre,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P86', 'P175', 'P136')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND c.domains LIKE '%music%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY i.label;


-- 6. Events of a period with where they happened and who took part.
SELECT i.label AS event,
       min(e.year) AS year,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P17'  THEN v.label END) AS country,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P276' THEN v.label END) AS location,
       string_agg(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.property = 'P710' THEN v.label END, ', ') AS participants
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P17', 'P276', 'P710')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1600 AND 1699
  AND c.domains LIKE '%event%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY year
LIMIT 50;


-- 7. Which occupations actually occur in the data.
--    This is the list to map onto areas (science, music, art) - far smaller
--    than the full occupation vocabulary, because only these are used.
SELECT v.label AS occupation, count(*) AS people
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY people DESC
LIMIT 200;


-- 8. Data quality.
--    Date precision: month = 0 means the source only knew the year.
SELECT p.label AS date_type,
       count(*) AS dates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.month = 0) AS year_only,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.bc)        AS bc,
       min(e.year) AS earliest,
       max(e.year) AS latest
FROM events e
JOIN properties p ON p.pid = e.property
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY dates DESC;

--    Attribute values that resolve_values.py could not label. Anything here
--    means the values file is stale against the extract.
SELECT a.property, count(*) AS unresolved
FROM attributes a
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE v.qid IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unresolved DESC;


-- 9. Works of a named creator.
--    Queries 5 and 6 attach attributes to show them, so they LEFT JOIN and
--    keep rows that have none. Here the attribute IS the filter, so it is an
--    inner JOIN and the name stands alone in the WHERE clause: a work with no
--    creator recorded must not come back. Softening this with
--    "OR a.property IS NULL" would let every work in the database through.
--    The three creator properties are tested together - which one a work uses
--    is not predictable: a book is P50, a symphony P86, a painting P170.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM items i
JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50', 'P86', 'P170')
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.qid = i.qid
WHERE v.label = 'Isaac Newton'
GROUP BY i.qid, i.label
ORDER BY year;


Turn the JSON structurial request below into a single DuckDB SQL SELECT statement that
answers it. Reply with ONLY the SQL - no markdown fences, no explanation.

How to read the request JSON:
- target_type is the kind of entity to return (person / event / work).
- answer_field is the projection. null -> return the matching entities. Name a person by
  coalesce(i.label, i.label_ru) - some items have only a non-English label - and when the query
  aggregates (string_agg/min over a person's several attribute rows) GROUP BY i.qid, never
  GROUP BY i.label (a NULL or shared label merges distinct people into one blank-named row).
  "time" -> return the target's year; "location" -> return the target's place. When it is
  non-null, SELECT that one attribute instead of the entity rows.
- filters.name -> the target is a specific named entity: match it by label, replacing the internal
  spaces with % so intervening words don't block the match - name "Symphony 5" ->
  i.label ILIKE '%Symphony%5%' (matches the stored "Symphony No. 5"), not '%Symphony 5%'.
- filters.related_entity {relation, entity_mention} -> a linked entity used to filter/disambiguate.
  "creates" is the person<->work edge: if target_type is "work", entity_mention is the creator; if
  "person", it is the work. Test the creator properties together in one condition, never pick one of
  them - which property a work uses is not predictable (Newton's books are P50/author, a symphony is
  P86/composer, a painting is P170/creator):
  JOIN attributes a ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50','P86','P170'),
  JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a."value", WHERE v."label" = '<entity_mention>'.
- filters.occupation -> the person's occupation, stored as attribute P106 and resolved through
  value_items: JOIN attributes a ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property = 'P106', JOIN value_items v ON
  v.qid = a.value, WHERE v.label = '<occupation>'. It is NOT a word in i.label - never write
  i.label LIKE '%composer%'.
- filters.location -> a place attribute (e.g. P27 country of citizenship, P19 place of birth for a
  person), resolved through value_items the same way; not a word in i.label. Match the resolved place
  name with a word-boundary regex - regexp_matches(v.label, '(?i)\b<place>') - rather than
  ILIKE '%<place>%', so "Russia" does not also match "Prussia"/"Byelorussia" (this still keeps
  "Russian Empire", "Tsardom of Russia").
- filters.domain -> the classes.domains tag, reached through BOTH joins, written out in full:
  JOIN item_classes l ON l.qid = i.qid, JOIN classes c ON c.qid = l."class", WHERE c.domains LIKE
  '%<domain>%'. Referencing c.domains without joining classes is an error, not a shortcut: every
  alias used anywhere in the query must appear in the FROM/JOIN list. It is NOT a word in i.label.
  domains holds '|'-separated tags from a closed set - art, event, literature, music, person, place,
  science - so a domain outside that set matches no row at all: map it to the nearest tag first
  ("mathematics", "physics", "chemistry" -> science; "jazz", "opera" -> music; "poetry" -> literature).
- filters.time_constraint -> a constraint on the target's date(s), which live in the events table
  (P569 date of birth, P570 date of death for a person; creation/publication year for a work/event).
  Pull a person's lifespan once in a CTE: max(year) FILTER (WHERE property='P569') AS born, and the
  same with P570 AS died. Its entity_mention (type relative_to_entity) is a TIME ANCHOR, not a
  creator - do NOT join P86/P50 for it.
    - type "in_range": WHERE year BETWEEN start_year AND end_year.
    - type "relative_to_entity": resolve the named anchor's born/died in a CTE first, then compare
      each candidate's lifespan to it - "overlap" -> born <= anchor.died AND died >= anchor.born;
      "before" -> died <= anchor.born; "after" -> born >= anchor.died. See the overlap example.
      Many items share a surname, so resolve the anchor to a dated person (born IS NOT NULL) and pick
      the most-documented one (ORDER BY (SELECT count(*) FROM attributes a WHERE a.qid=i.qid) DESC
      LIMIT 1); never LIMIT 1 on the bare label. Reference the single-row anchor as scalar subqueries
      - l.born <= (SELECT died FROM anchor) AND l.died >= (SELECT born FROM anchor) - so it needs no
      join in the main FROM and can't be dropped when you add other filters. When comparing lifespans,
      guard against impossible ones from bad death-years with AND died - born <= 110.
- filters.compare_entities -> a direct comparison between the listed named entities; resolve each
  entity's relevant attribute (lifespan, location, or work count) and compare them.
- Apply a condition for EVERY filter whose value is non-null, and only those. The example queries
  show how to express each filter type - they are patterns to combine, not templates to copy whole.
  When the request has several filters (e.g. occupation AND location AND time_constraint), the query
  must constrain on all of them; never copy the nearest example and silently drop a filter it doesn't
  happen to show. Leave any filter whose value is null out of the WHERE clause.

Keep the query minimal: include a table or join only when it feeds the SELECT list or a
WHERE/GROUP BY condition. When filters.domain is null, do not add item_classes/classes (or any other)
joins the request does not need - an unneeded INNER join can silently drop the answer rows (e.g. a
work with no class-closure membership). The rule cuts both ways: when filters.domain is non-null
those two joins ARE needed, and dropping them while keeping the c.domains condition does not make the
query minimal, it makes it invalid. Use the fewest tables that answer the request, and prefer
LEFT JOIN for anything not being filtered on.

A table you DO filter on is the opposite case: join it with JOIN, not LEFT JOIN, and let its
condition stand on its own. Never soften a filter with an escape hatch - no OR a.property IS NULL,
no OR v.label IS NULL, no COALESCE around the filtered column. Those look protective and are the
worst outcome available: every item that simply has no such attribute passes the test, so the filter
is switched off and the query answers with the whole table instead of the few rows asked for. If an
attribute filter is right, an item without that attribute must not be in the result. Put the
property list in the ON clause and the value test in the WHERE clause.

Check the query before replying: every alias in the SELECT list, WHERE clause and GROUP BY must be
defined in the FROM/JOIN list. In particular, if c.domains appears anywhere, then both
JOIN item_classes l ON l.qid = i.qid and JOIN classes c ON c.qid = l."class" must be in the query.
Add the missing join rather than dropping the condition, and start the FROM list from items i.
Check the filters too: no condition may contain OR ... IS NULL, and any attribute you filter on is
joined with JOIN rather than LEFT JOIN.

Request: {
  "target_type": "work",
  "answer_field": "time",
  "filters": {
    "name": "Symphony 5",
    "occupation": null,
    "location": null,
    "domain": "music",
    "time_constraint": null,
    "related_entity": {
      "relation": "creates",
      "entity_mention": "Beethoven"
    },
    "compare_entities": null
  }
}

```sql
SELECT coalesce(i."label", i.label_ru) AS work,
       (SELECT min(e.year) FROM events e WHERE e.qid = i.qid) AS year,
       (SELECT sitelinks FROM sites s WHERE s.qid = i.qid) AS sitelinks
FROM items i
WHERE (i."label" ILIKE '%Symphony%5%' OR i.label_ru ILIKE '%Symphony%5%')
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM item_classes l JOIN classes c ON c.qid = l."class" WHERE l.qid = i.qid AND c.domains LIKE '%music%')
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attributes a JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a."value" WHERE a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50', 'P86', 'P170', 'P175', 'P676') AND regexp_matches(v."label", '(?i)\bBeethoven'))
ORDER BY sitelinks DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 200;
```

-- 1. What happened in a given year in music and science.
--    Items are matched through every class they belong to, and classes carry
--    the domain tag assigned by build_class_closure.py.
SELECT i.label,
       i.description,
       c.label   AS class,
       c.domains AS area,
       p.label   AS date_type,
       e.year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
JOIN properties p   ON p.pid = e.property
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND (c.domains LIKE '%music%' OR c.domains LIKE '%science%')
ORDER BY c.domains, i.label;


-- 2. The same question asked over a whole century, counted by area.
SELECT (e.year / 100)::BIGINT * 100 AS century,
       c.domains AS area,
       count(DISTINCT e.qid) AS items
FROM events e
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1800 AND 1899
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY items DESC;


-- 3. Which scientists lived in Germany in the 1400s.
--    "Lived in" is read as born or died inside the window, which also keeps
--    people whose other date is unknown.
WITH lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
),
occupation AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS occupation
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P106'
),
citizenship AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS country
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P27'
)
-- a person usually has several occupations and sometimes several
-- citizenships, so collapse them instead of repeating the person per row
SELECT i.label,
       string_agg(DISTINCT o.occupation, ', ') AS occupations,
       string_agg(DISTINCT z.country, ', ')    AS countries,
       min(l.born) AS born,
       min(l.died) AS died
FROM lifespan l
JOIN items i      USING (qid)
JOIN occupation o USING (qid)
JOIN citizenship z USING (qid)
WHERE z.country ILIKE '%German%'
  -- "scientist" is an area, not a job title - only 50 people dated to this
  -- century carry it, against 2,039 professions that occupation_areas puts
  -- under science
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attributes a
              JOIN occupation_areas oa ON oa.qid = a."value"
              WHERE a.qid = l.qid AND a.property = 'P106'
                AND list_contains(str_split(oa.areas, '|'), 'science'))
  AND (l.born BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499 OR l.died BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499)
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY born;


-- 4. Anyone by occupation and period, the generic form of query 3.
--    Change the two parameters at the top and the rest follows.
WITH params AS (SELECT 'composer' AS want_occupation, 1700 AS from_year, 1799 AS to_year),
lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
)
SELECT i.label, v.label AS occupation, l.born, l.died
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
JOIN items i       ON i.qid = a.qid
JOIN lifespan l    ON l.qid = a.qid
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
  AND v.label = params.want_occupation
  AND l.born BETWEEN params.from_year AND params.to_year
ORDER BY l.born;


-- 5. Musical works of a year with the people and genre attached to them.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P86'  THEN v.label END) AS composer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P175' THEN v.label END) AS performer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P136' THEN v.label END) AS genre,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P86', 'P175', 'P136')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND c.domains LIKE '%music%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY i.label;


-- 6. Events of a period with where they happened and who took part.
SELECT i.label AS event,
       min(e.year) AS year,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P17'  THEN v.label END) AS country,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P276' THEN v.label END) AS location,
       string_agg(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.property = 'P710' THEN v.label END, ', ') AS participants
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P17', 'P276', 'P710')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1600 AND 1699
  AND c.domains LIKE '%event%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY year
LIMIT 50;


-- 7. Which occupations actually occur in the data.
--    This is the list to map onto areas (science, music, art) - far smaller
--    than the full occupation vocabulary, because only these are used.
SELECT v.label AS occupation, count(*) AS people
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY people DESC
LIMIT 200;


-- 8. Data quality.
--    Date precision: month = 0 means the source only knew the year.
SELECT p.label AS date_type,
       count(*) AS dates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.month = 0) AS year_only,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.bc)        AS bc,
       min(e.year) AS earliest,
       max(e.year) AS latest
FROM events e
JOIN properties p ON p.pid = e.property
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY dates DESC;

--    Attribute values that resolve_values.py could not label. Anything here
--    means the values file is stale against the extract.
SELECT a.property, count(*) AS unresolved
FROM attributes a
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE v.qid IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unresolved DESC;


-- 9. Works of a named creator.
--    Queries 5 and 6 attach attributes to show them, so they LEFT JOIN and
--    keep rows that have none. Here the attribute IS the filter, so it is an
--    inner JOIN and the name stands alone in the WHERE clause: a work with no
--    creator recorded must not come back. Softening this with
--    "OR a.property IS NULL" would let every work in the database through.
--    The three creator properties are tested together - which one a work uses
--    is not predictable: a book is P50, a symphony P86, a painting P170.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM items i
JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50', 'P86', 'P170')
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.qid = i.qid
WHERE v.label = 'Isaac Newton'
GROUP BY i.qid, i.label
ORDER BY year;

--
-- This is the structure load_duckdb.py builds out of the wpars output. The
-- loader creates the tables itself with CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT,
-- so this file is not needed to load data; it is the written-down model of the
-- result, and it stands up an empty database with the same tables for tooling
-- that expects them to exist.
--
-- Run it with the DuckDB CLI. The ATTACH names the database file, so the file
-- does not have to be on the command line - both of these end up in the same
-- place:
--
--   duckdb < db_model.sql              -- creates ./wiki.duckdb
--   duckdb wiki.duckdb < db_model.sql  -- same database, already open
--
-- Every table is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so running this against a loaded
-- database changes nothing and cannot drop rows.
--
-- The MySQL version of this model was replaced when the project moved to
-- DuckDB; it is in git history as `git show 7febd4b:db_model.sql`. Its column
-- widths no longer hold anyway - labels run past VARCHAR(30) and `year` needs
-- more than SMALLINT (see the note on events below).
--
-- No table carries a primary key, a foreign key or an index:
--   - the CSVs are the source of truth and every load rebuilds the tables, so
--     constraints would only slow the bulk load down;
--   - the workload is analytical (group by century, filter by occupation or
--     country, join events to items), which DuckDB answers by scanning columns
--     with zone maps rather than by seeking through an index.
-- The relationships are written in the comments instead. They hold: the
-- January extract had 0 orphans in events, attributes and item_classes.

ATTACH IF NOT EXISTS 'wiki.duckdb' AS wiki;
USE wiki;

-- Dictionaries
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per selected Wikidata item: everything that has at least one date
-- and belongs to at least one class of interest. Source: ItemsExt.csv.

    qid             VARCHAR,  -- Wikidata QID, e.g. Q42
    "label"         VARCHAR,  -- English label
    description     VARCHAR,
    label_ru        VARCHAR,  -- second language, see get_sites() in gconfig.h

);

    pid          VARCHAR,  -- e.g. P569

    description  VARCHAR,

);

-- The P31 whitelist: every class reachable from a seed through P279, tagged
-- with the domain(s) that seed belongs to. Built by build_class_closure.py.
-- Source: select_classes.csv.

    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR,
    domains      VARCHAR   -- '|' separated, e.g. 'event|literature|music'.
                           -- A closed set of seven tags, one per seed group:
                           -- art, event, literature, music, person, place,

    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid

    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P106'
),

    WHERE a.property = 'P27'

-- citizenships, so collapse them instead of repeating the person per row

       string_agg(DISTINCT o.occupation, ', ') AS occupations,
       string_agg(DISTINCT z.country, ', ')    AS countries,
       min(l.born) AS born,
       min(l.died) AS died
FROM lifespan l
JOIN items i      USING (qid)
JOIN occupation o USING (qid)
JOIN citizenship z USING (qid)

ORDER BY born;

WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1600 AND 1699

FROM attributes a

--   duckdb wiki.duckdb < db_model.sql  -- same database, already open
--
-- Every table is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so running this against a loaded
-- database changes nothing and cannot drop rows.

-- DuckDB; it is in git history as `git show 7febd4b:db_model.sql`. Its column
-- widths no longer hold anyway - labels run past VARCHAR(30) and `year` needs
-- more than SMALLINT (see the note on events below).

--   - the workload is analytical (group by century, filter by occupation or
--     country, join events to items), which DuckDB answers by scanning columns
--     with zone maps rather than by seeking through an index.
-- The relationships are written in the comments instead. They hold: the
-- January extract had 0 orphans in events, attributes and item_classes.

-- Dictionaries
-- -----------------------------------------------------

    qid             VARCHAR,  -- Wikidata QID, e.g. Q42

-- Source: select_classes.csv.

    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR,
    domains      VARCHAR   -- '|' separated, e.g. 'event|literature|music'.

                           -- science. Any other value matches nothing.
);

-- countries, places, genres). Resolved out of the full item dump by
-- resolve_values.py, because those items are not selected in their own right.
-- Source: values.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS value_items (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR
);

-- records a profession: the 15th century has 58,088 dated people, of whom 50
-- are labelled "scientist" and the rest are astronomers, physicians and
-- mathematicians. Built by build_occupation_areas.py from the P279 closure of a
-- few area roots, kept to the occupations the extract actually uses.
-- Source: occupation_areas.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS occupation_areas (
    qid          VARCHAR,  -- the QID a P106 attribute row points at
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. astronomer

    people       BIGINT    -- how many people in the extract hold it
);

-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per (item, date property, class) fact - the events the questions are
-- asked about. Source: DataEvents.csv, loaded with DISTINCT.
--
-- The Wikidata time string is kept as it arrived and also split into columns,
-- since the questions are about years and centuries.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    qid            VARCHAR,   -- -> items.qid
    property       VARCHAR,   -- -> properties.pid, e.g. P569 (date of birth)
    "class"        VARCHAR,   -- -> classes.qid

    property  VARCHAR,  -- -> properties.pid

-- Source: ItemSites.csv.

-- database changes nothing and cannot drop rows.

--     with zone maps rather than by seeking through an index.

-- January extract had 0 orphans in events, attributes and item_classes.

    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid

--   duckdb wiki.duckdb < db_model.sql  -- same database, already open

-- Dictionaries

-- Source: properties.json plus the two selection files.

-- Source: select_classes.csv.

    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR,

-- Facts
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- 1. What happened in a given year in music and science.
--    Items are matched through every class they belong to, and classes carry
--    the domain tag assigned by build_class_closure.py.
SELECT i.label,
       i.description,
       c.label   AS class,
       c.domains AS area,
       p.label   AS date_type,
       e.year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
JOIN properties p   ON p.pid = e.property
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND (c.domains LIKE '%music%' OR c.domains LIKE '%science%')
ORDER BY c.domains, i.label;


-- 2. The same question asked over a whole century, counted by area.
SELECT (e.year / 100)::BIGINT * 100 AS century,
       c.domains AS area,
       count(DISTINCT e.qid) AS items
FROM events e
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1800 AND 1899
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY items DESC;


-- 3. Which scientists lived in Germany in the 1400s.
--    "Lived in" is read as born or died inside the window, which also keeps
--    people whose other date is unknown.
WITH lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
),
occupation AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS occupation
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P106'
),
citizenship AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS country
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P27'
)
-- a person usually has several occupations and sometimes several
-- citizenships, so collapse them instead of repeating the person per row
SELECT i.label,
       string_agg(DISTINCT o.occupation, ', ') AS occupations,
       string_agg(DISTINCT z.country, ', ')    AS countries,
       min(l.born) AS born,
       min(l.died) AS died
FROM lifespan l
JOIN items i      USING (qid)
JOIN occupation o USING (qid)
JOIN citizenship z USING (qid)
WHERE z.country ILIKE '%German%'
  -- "scientist" is an area, not a job title - only 50 people dated to this
  -- century carry it, against 2,039 professions that occupation_areas puts
  -- under science
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attributes a
              JOIN occupation_areas oa ON oa.qid = a."value"
              WHERE a.qid = l.qid AND a.property = 'P106'
                AND list_contains(str_split(oa.areas, '|'), 'science'))
  AND (l.born BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499 OR l.died BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499)
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY born;


-- 4. Anyone by occupation and period, the generic form of query 3.
--    Change the two parameters at the top and the rest follows.
WITH params AS (SELECT 'composer' AS want_occupation, 1700 AS from_year, 1799 AS to_year),
lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
)
SELECT i.label, v.label AS occupation, l.born, l.died
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
JOIN items i       ON i.qid = a.qid
JOIN lifespan l    ON l.qid = a.qid
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
  AND v.label = params.want_occupation
  AND l.born BETWEEN params.from_year AND params.to_year
ORDER BY l.born;


-- 5. Musical works of a year with the people and genre attached to them.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P86'  THEN v.label END) AS composer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P175' THEN v.label END) AS performer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P136' THEN v.label END) AS genre,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P86', 'P175', 'P136')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND c.domains LIKE '%music%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY i.label;


-- 6. Events of a period with where they happened and who took part.
SELECT i.label AS event,
       min(e.year) AS year,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P17'  THEN v.label END) AS country,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P276' THEN v.label END) AS location,
       string_agg(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.property = 'P710' THEN v.label END, ', ') AS participants
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P17', 'P276', 'P710')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1600 AND 1699
  AND c.domains LIKE '%event%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY year
LIMIT 50;


-- 7. Which occupations actually occur in the data.
--    This is the list to map onto areas (science, music, art) - far smaller
--    than the full occupation vocabulary, because only these are used.
SELECT v.label AS occupation, count(*) AS people
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY people DESC
LIMIT 200;


-- 8. Data quality.
--    Date precision: month = 0 means the source only knew the year.
SELECT p.label AS date_type,
       count(*) AS dates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.month = 0) AS year_only,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.bc)        AS bc,
       min(e.year) AS earliest,
       max(e.year) AS latest
FROM events e
JOIN properties p ON p.pid = e.property
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY dates DESC;

--    means the values file is stale against the extract.

FROM attributes a
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE v.qid IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unresolved DESC;

--    Queries 5 and 6 attach attributes to show them, so they LEFT JOIN and
--    keep rows that have none. Here the attribute IS the filter, so it is an
--    inner JOIN and the name stands alone in the WHERE clause: a work with no
--    creator recorded must not come back. Softening this with
--    "OR a.property IS NULL" would let every work in the database through.
--    The three creator properties are tested together - which one a work uses

       min(e.year) AS year
FROM items i
JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50', 'P86', 'P170')
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.qid = i.qid
WHERE v.label = 'Isaac Newton'
GROUP BY i.qid, i.label
ORDER BY year;

USE wiki;

-- Dictionaries
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per selected Wikidata item: everything that has at least one date
-- and belongs to at least one class of interest. Source: ItemsExt.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (
    qid             VARCHAR,  -- Wikidata QID, e.g. Q42
    "label"         VARCHAR,  -- English label
    description     VARCHAR,
    label_ru        VARCHAR,  -- second language, see get_sites() in gconfig.h

-- Property dictionary, tagged with the role the property plays here.
-- Source: properties.json plus the two selection files.

    description  VARCHAR,
    kind         VARCHAR   -- 'date' | 'attribute' | 'other'
);

-- The P31 whitelist: every class reachable from a seed through P279, tagged
-- with the domain(s) that seed belongs to. Built by build_class_closure.py.
-- Source: select_classes.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS classes (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR,
    domains      VARCHAR   -- '|' separated, e.g. 'event|literature|music'.

                           -- science. Any other value matches nothing.
);

-- Labels for the QIDs that turn up as attribute values (occupations,
-- countries, places, genres). Resolved out of the full item dump by
-- resolve_values.py, because those items are not selected in their own right.
-- Source: values.csv.

    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR
);

-- few area roots, kept to the occupations the extract actually uses.
-- Source: occupation_areas.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS occupation_areas (
    qid          VARCHAR,  -- the QID a P106 attribute row points at
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. astronomer
    areas        VARCHAR,  -- '|' separated: art, literature, music, science
    people       BIGINT    -- how many people in the extract hold it
);

-- Facts
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per (item, date property, class) fact - the events the questions are
-- asked about. Source: DataEvents.csv, loaded with DISTINCT.
--
-- The Wikidata time string is kept as it arrived and also split into columns,
-- since the questions are about years and centuries.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    qid            VARCHAR,   -- -> items.qid
    property       VARCHAR,   -- -> properties.pid, e.g. P569 (date of birth)
    "class"        VARCHAR,   -- -> classes.qid

    "day"          UTINYINT,  -- 0 when the source has no day precision

-- with three occupations has three rows. Source: Attributes.csv, DISTINCT.

    qid       VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    property  VARCHAR,  -- -> properties.pid
    "value"   VARCHAR   -- -> value_items.qid
);

-- normally an instance of several classes, and a question can arrive through
-- any of them. Source: ItemClasses.csv, DISTINCT.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS item_classes (
    qid      VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    "class"  VARCHAR   -- -> classes.qid
);

-- answers - it is the only one the dump offers - and the titles are the join
-- key to article text, should the Wikipedia dataset be pulled in later.
-- Source: ItemSites.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sites (
    qid        VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    sitelinks  INTEGER,  -- number of Wikipedia editions holding the item
    enwiki     VARCHAR,  -- English article title, NULL when there is none
    ruwiki     VARCHAR   -- Russian article title, NULL when there is none
);

FROM duckdb_tables()
WHERE database_name = 'wiki'
ORDER BY table_name;

-- Tables: items, events, attributes, item_classes, sites, value_items,
-- classes, occupation_areas, properties - the model is in db_model.sql.
-- Queries 1 and 2 run on any build; the rest need attributes and item_classes,
-- which only exist after a run made with --attrs.


-- 1. What happened in a given year in music and science.
--    Items are matched through every class they belong to, and classes carry
--    the domain tag assigned by build_class_closure.py.
SELECT i.label,
       i.description,
       c.label   AS class,
       c.domains AS area,
       p.label   AS date_type,
       e.year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
JOIN properties p   ON p.pid = e.property
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND (c.domains LIKE '%music%' OR c.domains LIKE '%science%')
ORDER BY c.domains, i.label;


-- 2. The same question asked over a whole century, counted by area.
SELECT (e.year / 100)::BIGINT * 100 AS century,
       c.domains AS area,
       count(DISTINCT e.qid) AS items
FROM events e
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1800 AND 1899
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY items DESC;


-- 3. Which scientists lived in Germany in the 1400s.
--    "Lived in" is read as born or died inside the window, which also keeps
--    people whose other date is unknown.
WITH lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
),
occupation AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS occupation
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P106'
),
citizenship AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS country
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P27'
)
-- a person usually has several occupations and sometimes several
-- citizenships, so collapse them instead of repeating the person per row
SELECT i.label,
       string_agg(DISTINCT o.occupation, ', ') AS occupations,
       string_agg(DISTINCT z.country, ', ')    AS countries,
       min(l.born) AS born,
       min(l.died) AS died
FROM lifespan l
JOIN items i      USING (qid)
JOIN occupation o USING (qid)
JOIN citizenship z USING (qid)
WHERE z.country ILIKE '%German%'
  -- "scientist" is an area, not a job title - only 50 people dated to this
  -- century carry it, against 2,039 professions that occupation_areas puts
  -- under science
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attributes a
              JOIN occupation_areas oa ON oa.qid = a."value"
              WHERE a.qid = l.qid AND a.property = 'P106'
                AND list_contains(str_split(oa.areas, '|'), 'science'))
  AND (l.born BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499 OR l.died BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499)
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY born;


-- 4. Anyone by occupation and period, the generic form of query 3.
--    Change the two parameters at the top and the rest follows.
WITH params AS (SELECT 'composer' AS want_occupation, 1700 AS from_year, 1799 AS to_year),
lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
)
SELECT i.label, v.label AS occupation, l.born, l.died
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
JOIN items i       ON i.qid = a.qid
JOIN lifespan l    ON l.qid = a.qid
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
  AND v.label = params.want_occupation
  AND l.born BETWEEN params.from_year AND params.to_year
ORDER BY l.born;


-- 5. Musical works of a year with the people and genre attached to them.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P86'  THEN v.label END) AS composer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P175' THEN v.label END) AS performer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P136' THEN v.label END) AS genre,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P86', 'P175', 'P136')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND c.domains LIKE '%music%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY i.label;


-- 6. Events of a period with where they happened and who took part.
SELECT i.label AS event,
       min(e.year) AS year,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P17'  THEN v.label END) AS country,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P276' THEN v.label END) AS location,
       string_agg(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.property = 'P710' THEN v.label END, ', ') AS participants
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P17', 'P276', 'P710')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1600 AND 1699
  AND c.domains LIKE '%event%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY year
LIMIT 50;


-- 7. Which occupations actually occur in the data.
--    This is the list to map onto areas (science, music, art) - far smaller
--    than the full occupation vocabulary, because only these are used.
SELECT v.label AS occupation, count(*) AS people
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY people DESC
LIMIT 200;


-- 8. Data quality.
--    Date precision: month = 0 means the source only knew the year.
SELECT p.label AS date_type,
       count(*) AS dates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.month = 0) AS year_only,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.bc)        AS bc,
       min(e.year) AS earliest,
       max(e.year) AS latest
FROM events e
JOIN properties p ON p.pid = e.property
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY dates DESC;

--    Attribute values that resolve_values.py could not label. Anything here
--    means the values file is stale against the extract.
SELECT a.property, count(*) AS unresolved
FROM attributes a
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE v.qid IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unresolved DESC;


-- 9. Works of a named creator.
--    Queries 5 and 6 attach attributes to show them, so they LEFT JOIN and
--    keep rows that have none. Here the attribute IS the filter, so it is an
--    inner JOIN and the name stands alone in the WHERE clause: a work with no
--    creator recorded must not come back. Softening this with
--    "OR a.property IS NULL" would let every work in the database through.
--    The three creator properties are tested together - which one a work uses
--    is not predictable: a book is P50, a symphony P86, a painting P170.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM items i
JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50', 'P86', 'P170')
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.qid = i.qid
WHERE v.label = 'Isaac Newton'
GROUP BY i.qid, i.label
ORDER BY year;

-- 1. What happened in a given year in music and science.
--    Items are matched through every class they belong to, and classes carry
--    the domain tag assigned by build_class_closure.py.
SELECT i.label,
       i.description,
       c.label   AS class,
       c.domains AS area,
       p.label   AS date_type,
       e.year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
JOIN properties p   ON p.pid = e.property
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND (c.domains LIKE '%music%' OR c.domains LIKE '%science%')
ORDER BY c.domains, i.label;


-- 2. The same question asked over a whole century, counted by area.
SELECT (e.year / 100)::BIGINT * 100 AS century,
       c.domains AS area,
       count(DISTINCT e.qid) AS items
FROM events e
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1800 AND 1899
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY items DESC;


-- 3. Which scientists lived in Germany in the 1400s.
--    "Lived in" is read as born or died inside the window, which also keeps
--    people whose other date is unknown.
WITH lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
),
occupation AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS occupation
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P106'
),
citizenship AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS country
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P27'
)
-- a person usually has several occupations and sometimes several
-- citizenships, so collapse them instead of repeating the person per row
SELECT i.label,
       string_agg(DISTINCT o.occupation, ', ') AS occupations,
       string_agg(DISTINCT z.country, ', ')    AS countries,
       min(l.born) AS born,
       min(l.died) AS died
FROM lifespan l
JOIN items i      USING (qid)
JOIN occupation o USING (qid)
JOIN citizenship z USING (qid)
WHERE z.country ILIKE '%German%'
  -- "scientist" is an area, not a job title - only 50 people dated to this
  -- century carry it, against 2,039 professions that occupation_areas puts
  -- under science
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attributes a
              JOIN occupation_areas oa ON oa.qid = a."value"
              WHERE a.qid = l.qid AND a.property = 'P106'
                AND list_contains(str_split(oa.areas, '|'), 'science'))
  AND (l.born BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499 OR l.died BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499)
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY born;

--    Change the two parameters at the top and the rest follows.
WITH params AS (SELECT 'composer' AS want_occupation, 1700 AS from_year, 1799 AS to_year),
lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
)
SELECT i.label, v.label AS occupation, l.born, l.died
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
JOIN items i       ON i.qid = a.qid
JOIN lifespan l    ON l.qid = a.qid
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
  AND v.label = params.want_occupation
  AND l.born BETWEEN params.from_year AND params.to_year
ORDER BY l.born;


-- 5. Musical works of a year with the people and genre attached to them.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P86'  THEN v.label END) AS composer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P175' THEN v.label END) AS performer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P136' THEN v.label END) AS genre,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P86', 'P175', 'P136')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND c.domains LIKE '%music%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY i.label;


-- 6. Events of a period with where they happened and who took part.
SELECT i.label AS event,
       min(e.year) AS year,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P17'  THEN v.label END) AS country,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P276' THEN v.label END) AS location,
       string_agg(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.property = 'P710' THEN v.label END, ', ') AS participants
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P17', 'P276', 'P710')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1600 AND 1699
  AND c.domains LIKE '%event%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY year
LIMIT 50;


-- 7. Which occupations actually occur in the data.

--    than the full occupation vocabulary, because only these are used.

FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY people DESC
LIMIT 200;


-- 8. Data quality.
--    Date precision: month = 0 means the source only knew the year.
SELECT p.label AS date_type,
       count(*) AS dates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.month = 0) AS year_only,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.bc)        AS bc,
       min(e.year) AS earliest,
       max(e.year) AS latest
FROM events e
JOIN properties p ON p.pid = e.property
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY dates DESC;

--    means the values file is stale against the extract.

FROM attributes a
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE v.qid IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unresolved DESC;


-- 9. Works of a named creator.
--    Queries 5 and 6 attach attributes to show them, so they LEFT JOIN and
--    keep rows that have none. Here the attribute IS the filter, so it is an
--    inner JOIN and the name stands alone in the WHERE clause: a work with no
--    creator recorded must not come back. Softening this with
--    "OR a.property IS NULL" would let every work in the database through.
--    The three creator properties are tested together - which one a work uses

       min(e.year) AS year
FROM items i
JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50', 'P86', 'P170')
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.qid = i.qid
WHERE v.label = 'Isaac Newton'
GROUP BY i.qid, i.label
ORDER BY year;

-- 1. What happened in a given year in music and science.
--    Items are matched through every class they belong to, and classes carry
--    the domain tag assigned by build_class_closure.py.
SELECT i.label,
       i.description,
       c.label   AS class,
       c.domains AS area,
       p.label   AS date_type,
       e.year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
JOIN properties p   ON p.pid = e.property
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND (c.domains LIKE '%music%' OR c.domains LIKE '%science%')
ORDER BY c.domains, i.label;


-- 2. The same question asked over a whole century, counted by area.
SELECT (e.year / 100)::BIGINT * 100 AS century,
       c.domains AS area,
       count(DISTINCT e.qid) AS items
FROM events e
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1800 AND 1899
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY items DESC;


-- 3. Which scientists lived in Germany in the 1400s.
--    "Lived in" is read as born or died inside the window, which also keeps
--    people whose other date is unknown.
WITH lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
),
occupation AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS occupation
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P106'
),
citizenship AS (
    SELECT a.qid, v.label AS country
    FROM attributes a
    JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
    WHERE a.property = 'P27'
)
-- a person usually has several occupations and sometimes several
-- citizenships, so collapse them instead of repeating the person per row
SELECT i.label,
       string_agg(DISTINCT o.occupation, ', ') AS occupations,
       string_agg(DISTINCT z.country, ', ')    AS countries,
       min(l.born) AS born,
       min(l.died) AS died
FROM lifespan l
JOIN items i      USING (qid)
JOIN occupation o USING (qid)
JOIN citizenship z USING (qid)
WHERE z.country ILIKE '%German%'
  -- "scientist" is an area, not a job title - only 50 people dated to this
  -- century carry it, against 2,039 professions that occupation_areas puts
  -- under science
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attributes a
              JOIN occupation_areas oa ON oa.qid = a."value"
              WHERE a.qid = l.qid AND a.property = 'P106'
                AND list_contains(str_split(oa.areas, '|'), 'science'))
  AND (l.born BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499 OR l.died BETWEEN 1400 AND 1499)
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY born;


-- 4. Anyone by occupation and period, the generic form of query 3.
--    Change the two parameters at the top and the rest follows.
WITH params AS (SELECT 'composer' AS want_occupation, 1700 AS from_year, 1799 AS to_year),
lifespan AS (
    SELECT qid,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P569') AS born,
           max(year) FILTER (WHERE property = 'P570') AS died
    FROM events
    GROUP BY qid
)
SELECT i.label, v.label AS occupation, l.born, l.died
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
JOIN items i       ON i.qid = a.qid
JOIN lifespan l    ON l.qid = a.qid
CROSS JOIN params
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
  AND v.label = params.want_occupation
  AND l.born BETWEEN params.from_year AND params.to_year
ORDER BY l.born;


-- 5. Musical works of a year with the people and genre attached to them.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P86'  THEN v.label END) AS composer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P175' THEN v.label END) AS performer,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P136' THEN v.label END) AS genre,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P86', 'P175', 'P136')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year = 1875
  AND c.domains LIKE '%music%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY i.label;


-- 6. Events of a period with where they happened and who took part.
SELECT i.label AS event,
       min(e.year) AS year,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P17'  THEN v.label END) AS country,
       max(CASE WHEN a.property = 'P276' THEN v.label END) AS location,
       string_agg(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.property = 'P710' THEN v.label END, ', ') AS participants
FROM events e
JOIN items i        USING (qid)
JOIN item_classes l USING (qid)
JOIN classes c      ON c.qid = l."class"
LEFT JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = e.qid AND a.property IN ('P17', 'P276', 'P710')
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE e.year BETWEEN 1600 AND 1699
  AND c.domains LIKE '%event%'
GROUP BY i.label
ORDER BY year
LIMIT 50;


-- 7. Which occupations actually occur in the data.
--    This is the list to map onto areas (science, music, art) - far smaller
--    than the full occupation vocabulary, because only these are used.
SELECT v.label AS occupation, count(*) AS people
FROM attributes a
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE a.property = 'P106'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY people DESC
LIMIT 200;


-- 8. Data quality.
--    Date precision: month = 0 means the source only knew the year.
SELECT p.label AS date_type,
       count(*) AS dates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.month = 0) AS year_only,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.bc)        AS bc,
       min(e.year) AS earliest,
       max(e.year) AS latest
FROM events e
JOIN properties p ON p.pid = e.property
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY dates DESC;

--    Attribute values that resolve_values.py could not label. Anything here
--    means the values file is stale against the extract.
SELECT a.property, count(*) AS unresolved
FROM attributes a
LEFT JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
WHERE v.qid IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unresolved DESC;


-- 9. Works of a named creator.
--    Queries 5 and 6 attach attributes to show them, so they LEFT JOIN and
--    keep rows that have none. Here the attribute IS the filter, so it is an
--    inner JOIN and the name stands alone in the WHERE clause: a work with no
--    creator recorded must not come back. Softening this with
--    "OR a.property IS NULL" would let every work in the database through.
--    The three creator properties are tested together - which one a work uses
--    is not predictable: a book is P50, a symphony P86, a painting P170.
SELECT i.label AS work,
       min(e.year) AS year
FROM items i
JOIN attributes a  ON a.qid = i.qid AND a.property IN ('P50', 'P86', 'P170')
JOIN value_items v ON v.qid = a.value
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.qid = i.qid
WHERE v.label = 'Isaac Newton'
GROUP BY i.qid, i.label
ORDER BY year;

-- WiKi database model - DuckDB.
--
-- This is the structure load_duckdb.py builds out of the wpars output. The
-- loader creates the tables itself with CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT,
-- so this file is not needed to load data; it is the written-down model of the
-- result, and it stands up an empty database with the same tables for tooling
-- that expects them to exist.
--
-- Run it with the DuckDB CLI. The ATTACH names the database file, so the file
-- does not have to be on the command line - both of these end up in the same
-- place:
--
--   duckdb < db_model.sql              -- creates ./wiki.duckdb
--   duckdb wiki.duckdb < db_model.sql  -- same database, already open
--
-- Every table is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so running this against a loaded
-- database changes nothing and cannot drop rows.
--
-- The MySQL version of this model was replaced when the project moved to
-- DuckDB; it is in git history as `git show 7febd4b:db_model.sql`. Its column
-- widths no longer hold anyway - labels run past VARCHAR(30) and `year` needs
-- more than SMALLINT (see the note on events below).
--
-- No table carries a primary key, a foreign key or an index:
--   - the CSVs are the source of truth and every load rebuilds the tables, so
--     constraints would only slow the bulk load down;
--   - the workload is analytical (group by century, filter by occupation or
--     country, join events to items), which DuckDB answers by scanning columns
--     with zone maps rather than by seeking through an index.
-- The relationships are written in the comments instead. They hold: the
-- January extract had 0 orphans in events, attributes and item_classes.

ATTACH IF NOT EXISTS 'wiki.duckdb' AS wiki;
USE wiki;


-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- Dictionaries
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per selected Wikidata item: everything that has at least one date
-- and belongs to at least one class of interest. Source: ItemsExt.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (
    qid             VARCHAR,  -- Wikidata QID, e.g. Q42
    "label"         VARCHAR,  -- English label
    description     VARCHAR,
    label_ru        VARCHAR,  -- second language, see get_sites() in gconfig.h
    description_ru  VARCHAR
);

-- Property dictionary, tagged with the role the property plays here.
-- Source: properties.json plus the two selection files.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS properties (
    pid          VARCHAR,  -- e.g. P569
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. date of birth
    description  VARCHAR,
    kind         VARCHAR   -- 'date' | 'attribute' | 'other'
);

-- The P31 whitelist: every class reachable from a seed through P279, tagged
-- with the domain(s) that seed belongs to. Built by build_class_closure.py.
-- Source: select_classes.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS classes (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR,
    domains      VARCHAR   -- '|' separated, e.g. 'event|literature|music'.
                           -- A closed set of seven tags, one per seed group:
                           -- art, event, literature, music, person, place,
                           -- science. Any other value matches nothing.
);

-- Labels for the QIDs that turn up as attribute values (occupations,
-- countries, places, genres). Resolved out of the full item dump by
-- resolve_values.py, because those items are not selected in their own right.
-- Source: values.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS value_items (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR
);


-- Which area each occupation belongs to. A question says "scientists" and P106
-- records a profession: the 15th century has 58,088 dated people, of whom 50
-- are labelled "scientist" and the rest are astronomers, physicians and
-- mathematicians. Built by build_occupation_areas.py from the P279 closure of a
-- few area roots, kept to the occupations the extract actually uses.
-- Source: occupation_areas.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS occupation_areas (
    qid          VARCHAR,  -- the QID a P106 attribute row points at
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. astronomer
    areas        VARCHAR,  -- '|' separated: art, literature, music, science
    people       BIGINT    -- how many people in the extract hold it
);


-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- Facts
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per (item, date property, class) fact - the events the questions are
-- asked about. Source: DataEvents.csv, loaded with DISTINCT.
--
-- The Wikidata time string is kept as it arrived and also split into columns,
-- since the questions are about years and centuries.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    qid            VARCHAR,   -- -> items.qid
    property       VARCHAR,   -- -> properties.pid, e.g. P569 (date of birth)
    "class"        VARCHAR,   -- -> classes.qid
    time_raw       VARCHAR,   -- as in the dump, e.g. +1991-02-12T00:00:00Z
    "year"         BIGINT,    -- signed. Not SMALLINT: 40 rows in the January
                              -- extract were already outside 16 bits. Not even
                              -- INTEGER: the Big Bang is -13800000000.
    "month"        UTINYINT,  -- 0 when the source has no month precision
    "day"          UTINYINT,  -- 0 when the source has no day precision
    bc             BOOLEAN,   -- true for a negative year, e.g. Caesar -0044
    timezone       INTEGER,
    qual_property  VARCHAR,   -- claim qualifier, nullable
    qual_value     VARCHAR    -- nullable
);

-- Non-date claims: occupation, citizenship, place of birth, genre and the rest
-- of attribute_properties.csv. One row per (item, property, value) - an item
-- with three occupations has three rows. Source: Attributes.csv, DISTINCT.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attributes (
    qid       VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    property  VARCHAR,  -- -> properties.pid
    "value"   VARCHAR   -- -> value_items.qid
);

-- Which classes an item belongs to. Separate from events because an item is
-- normally an instance of several classes, and a question can arrive through
-- any of them. Source: ItemClasses.csv, DISTINCT.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS item_classes (
    qid      VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    "class"  VARCHAR   -- -> classes.qid
);

-- Wikipedia presence per item. sitelinks is the notability signal used to rank
-- answers - it is the only one the dump offers - and the titles are the join
-- key to article text, should the Wikipedia dataset be pulled in later.
-- Source: ItemSites.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sites (
    qid        VARCHAR,  -- -> items.qid
    sitelinks  INTEGER,  -- number of Wikipedia editions holding the item
    enwiki     VARCHAR,  -- English article title, NULL when there is none
    ruwiki     VARCHAR   -- Russian article title, NULL when there is none
);


-- What the database holds now. Zero rows everywhere means the tables were just
-- created and the loader has not run yet.
SELECT table_name, estimated_size AS rows, column_count AS columns
FROM duckdb_tables()
WHERE database_name = 'wiki'
ORDER BY table_name;

--   duckdb wiki.duckdb < db_model.sql  -- same database, already open
--

-- database changes nothing and cannot drop rows.

--   - the workload is analytical (group by century, filter by occupation or
--     country, join events to items), which DuckDB answers by scanning columns
--     with zone maps rather than by seeking through an index.
-- The relationships are written in the comments instead. They hold: the
-- January extract had 0 orphans in events, attributes and item_classes.

USE wiki;


-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- Dictionaries
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per selected Wikidata item: everything that has at least one date
-- and belongs to at least one class of interest. Source: ItemsExt.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (
    qid             VARCHAR,  -- Wikidata QID, e.g. Q42
    "label"         VARCHAR,  -- English label
    description     VARCHAR,
    label_ru        VARCHAR,  -- second language, see get_sites() in gconfig.h
    description_ru  VARCHAR
);

-- Property dictionary, tagged with the role the property plays here.
-- Source: properties.json plus the two selection files.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS properties (
    pid          VARCHAR,  -- e.g. P569
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. date of birth
    description  VARCHAR,
    kind         VARCHAR   -- 'date' | 'attribute' | 'other'
);

-- The P31 whitelist: every class reachable from a seed through P279, tagged
-- with the domain(s) that seed belongs to. Built by build_class_closure.py.
-- Source: select_classes.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS classes (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR,
    domains      VARCHAR   -- '|' separated, e.g. 'event|literature|music'.
                           -- A closed set of seven tags, one per seed group:

                           -- science. Any other value matches nothing.
);

-- countries, places, genres). Resolved out of the full item dump by
-- resolve_values.py, because those items are not selected in their own right.
-- Source: values.csv.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS value_items (
    qid          VARCHAR,
    "label"      VARCHAR,
    description  VARCHAR
);

    qid          VARCHAR,  -- the QID a P106 attribute row points at
    "label"      VARCHAR,  -- e.g. astronomer
    areas        VARCHAR,  -- '|' separated: art, literature, music, science
    people       BIGINT    -- how many people in the extract hold it
);


-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- Facts
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- One row per (item, date property, class) fact - the events the questions are
-- asked about. Source: DataEvents.csv, loaded with DISTINCT.
--

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (

    property       VARCHAR,   -- -> properties.pid, e.g. P569 (date of birth)

    property  VARCHAR,  -- -> properties.pid

);

    "class"  VARCHAR   -- -> classes.qid

);

WHERE database_name = 'wiki'
ORDER BY table_name;
